# Zamborin Games

> A small independent studio building free, instantly-playable games for the browser. Vanilla HTML/JavaScript/Canvas, no engines, no downloads, no logins. Hosted at zamborin.com.

## Games

- [Orbit](https://zamborin.com/orbit/): Ring-spinning light puzzle. Concentric rings carry broken arc-track; spin each ring (drag, or tap to nudge one step) so light runs from the hub out to every bulb on the rim, resolving into a symmetric mandala. A join only carries light when the ring is exactly in true. Later levels gear pairs of rings so turning one turns its partner the opposite way. Scored on level depth and how close to par you finish.
- [Bloom](https://zamborin.com/bloom/): Pipe-rotating irrigation puzzle. Water starts at a tap in the middle of the garden and the ground is tangled with pipes facing the wrong way. Tap a pipe to rotate it 90°; watered pipes turn blue, and a flower opens only once water reaches it. Every board is generated as a connected layout, so a solution always exists.
- [Untangle](https://zamborin.com/untangle/): Daily planar-graph puzzle. Drag the dots so no edges cross. Endless levels from Tutorial to Master; same puzzle for everyone today (daily seed).
- [Tessera](https://zamborin.com/tessera/): Endless falling-letter word puzzle. Tap a column to slide the tile; double-tap to drop it instantly. Form English words across or down, 3 letters minimum. Longer words score exponentially more. The game gets faster the longer you survive.
- [Socket](https://zamborin.com/socket/): Power-strip packing puzzle. A wall board of sockets and a pile of awkward plugs, all of which must be on at once. A plug occupies one socket but its body covers however many its moulding is wide, so a fat plug denies neighbours it does not sit in, and every lead comes in from off the wall with a fixed reach that limits which rows it can even attempt. Pick a plug up and the board shows which sockets it can reach.
- [Sluice](https://zamborin.com/sluice/): Sliding pipe puzzle. A grid of pipe with a tap and a ring of flowers on the border. You never rotate a piece: you drag a whole row or column and it slides as one, wrapping around so what leaves one edge re-enters at the other. Rows and columns cross, so nothing can be fixed a piece at a time. One solution per board.
- [Fold](https://zamborin.com/fold/): Origami folding puzzle. Each level is a creased sheet carrying pairs of coloured marks — a solid dot and a matching ring. Tap a crease and the smaller flap folds over onto the rest of the sheet, flipping its marks and stacking them on the layer beneath. Solve by landing every dot on its ring. Undo steps back one fold at a time.
- [Mobile](https://zamborin.com/mobile/): Balancing-sculpture puzzle in the spirit of Alexander Calder. Rods hang from rods; from their ends hang cut-paper shapes drawn from a tray. A rod is level when weight times arm length matches on both sides, so a heavy shape hung close in balances a light one hung far out. Weight is area, which means it is judged by eye rather than read off a number, and an unbalanced arm droops on its heavy side until corrected. Nothing to race and no way to lose.
- [Tailwind](https://zamborin.com/tailwind/): Catapult distance game. A rubber-band slingshot mounted on a forked post flings an aeroplane, which climbs, settles into a glide, touches down and rolls to a stop; distance is counted where it stops. Two inputs, neither of them dialled in: the first tap starts the band drawing back and a second tap fixes the force, then the whole catapult — band and aeroplane as one rigid piece — swings about its screw until a third tap releases, which fixes the launch angle. Both sweeps run fast enough that the good band is roughly 45-65 milliseconds wide, so knowing the right launch and landing it are separate skills. Six aircraft are offered, each showing weight, lift, drag and strength, and they are balanced to reach within a few per cent of the same distance by DIFFERENT launches rather than ranked. Reaching launch speed over a short stroke is a load of tens of g, so every airframe has a draw beyond which the wing strains and permanently loses lift and gains drag for that flight — the best draw runs from about half on the lightest to nearly full on the strongest. Aiming straight up loses, because the aeroplane arrives at the top with no flying speed and falls before it can glide. A wind is rolled fresh each attempt and shown on a dial before the player touches the band; it moves the best angle from high in still air down to shallow in a strong headwind, and it changes which aircraft is fastest — light ones in calm air, heavy ones in a gale. Deterministic apart from the wind. A best distance is kept per aircraft.
- [Stained](https://zamborin.com/stained/): Colour-mixing glass puzzle. A dark window and a bench of translucent coloured panes, laid over each other so that where they overlap the colours mix. Mixing is PIGMENT, not light: red and yellow make orange, yellow and blue make green, blue and red make purple, all three make brown, and because a cell's colour is the union of the panes covering it, order never matters. The central decision is what the goal reveals: it shows ONLY the overlaps, meaning where colours must mix and what into, and hides the single-colour glass entirely. So a coloured square on the goal is a clue rather than an instruction, and everywhere else the player may do as they like provided they make no overlap that was not asked for. Some panes arrive already secondary and so carry two primaries at once, and the CAMPAIGN RAMP IS BUILT ON WITHDRAWING THEM: a secondary pane hands the player a mixed colour for free, so an orange cell can be satisfied with no crossing at all, and stripping them means every mixed cell must be earned by a real overlap. Fewer secondary panes therefore makes a board harder, not easier. A physical switch under the window lights it and falls dark a second after release, so checking your work is a deliberate act rather than a permanent view. 100 levels in 14 tiers, from a six by six window with two panes to an eight by eight with fifteen; each board's difficulty was measured individually and selected into its tier, so the ramp is monotone. Progress is kept in the browser. Every level is built by scrambling a solved arrangement, so a solution always exists.
- [Prism](https://zamborin.com/prism/): Light-routing colour puzzle. A lamp fires one white beam across a grid; a prism splits it into red, yellow and blue, but only for light arriving head on at its flat face, and light striking a slanted side is scattered and lost. Red carries straight on, yellow bends left, blue bends right. The board arrives EMPTY: the player is given a counted-out set of mirrors, which turn a beam ninety degrees, and splitters, which turn half of it and let the rest carry straight on so one beam becomes two. Deciding where to place them is the puzzle. Colours mix like pigment rather than light, so red and yellow make orange, red and blue make purple, and yellow and blue make green; a gem wanting a secondary needs two beams arriving at it together, and stays dark until both are right. Opaque blocks absorb any beam that reaches them. Every board is built around a working light path and re-simulated before it is served, so a solution always exists.
- [Needle](https://zamborin.com/needle/): Threading and crossing puzzle. Pairs of coloured pins sit on a cloth and each pair is joined by dragging its thread between them. The twist inverts the usual rule of the genre: threads are REQUIRED to cross rather than forbidden from it. A thread that meets nothing is lying on the surface, not sewn in, and is drawn drained of colour and floating above the cloth. Each thread must cross at least two others from level 3, one on levels 1 and 2. Each colour also has a single button its own thread must pass through, so the direct route is rarely the answer. A cell carries one horizontal pass and one vertical pass, which is what a crossing is; a thread that turns takes the whole cell. A Hint button lays one thread exactly where the answer puts it.
- [Zood](https://zamborin.com/zood/): Bubble-shooter arcade. Aim the cannon (mouse on desktop, drag on mobile) and fire character tiles at the cluster hanging above; match three or more of a kind to burst them, and any Zoods left dangling drop away too. Bank shots off the side walls to reach gaps you cannot hit head-on, and keep the cluster from reaching the line.
- [Carrom](https://zamborin.com/carrom/): Digital take on the South-Asian tabletop classic. Flick the striker, pocket your discs. Three difficulty levels against the computer.
- [Ludo](https://zamborin.com/ludo/): 2, 3, or 4-player Ludo board game. Roll two dice, split the count, capture opponents off safe squares. Daily seed shared across all players.

## Pages

- [Guides](https://zamborin.com/guides/): Strategy guides and how-to-play walkthroughs. One per game for Orbit, Bloom, Untangle, Tessera, Socket, Sluice, Fold, Mobile, Prism, Needle, Tailwind, Stained, Zood, Carrom and Ludo.
- [About](https://zamborin.com/about/): What Zamborin Games is and how the studio works.
- [FAQ](https://zamborin.com/faq/): Whether the games are free, whether an account is needed, mobile support, how the site makes money, and what data is collected.
- [Privacy](https://zamborin.com/privacy/): What data the site collects (almost none) and how Google AdSense cookies are used.
- [Contact](https://zamborin.com/contact/): Contact form for bug reports, feedback, partnerships.

## Background

The studio is run lean — small games shipped end-to-end by one or two people, no engine dependencies, no build pipeline. Every game is a folder of static HTML / JavaScript / CSS deployed via Vercel from a single git repository. Shared assets (audio engine, input helpers, design tokens) live in a `/shared/` toolkit.

The site is free to play and supported by Google AdSense. EU/UK/Switzerland visitors see a consent banner; everyone else sees ads without the prompt.
